trigger: a future reorder or insertion into kSparkMetricTokens[] without updating agent_registry.cpp's hand-indexed [mi][0..3] read loop
summary: agent_registry.cpp's recompute_metrics reader loop indexes kSparkMetricTokens[] by bare literal (0/1/2/3), bound to the array's declared order only by a comment - a future reorder would still compile but silently misattribute one health signal's fleet sum into another gauge family, corrupting the family backing the CRITICAL YuzuSparkMechanismQuarantined alert. Three independent reporters converged on this same underlying defect at increasing depth: security-guardian (Gate 2, INFO - noted as a pre-existing pattern merely extended), architect (Gate 3, NICE/LOW - recommended a static_assert pinning array size), and consistency-auditor (Gate 4, SHOULD/MEDIUM - the sharpest derivation, tracing the corrupted family to a CRITICAL-severity alert). Per the derivation rule the strongest read governs: SHOULD.

Fixed in 5bcd8df63: named indices (kSparkMetricIdxWatchRejected etc.) + pointer-identity static_asserts pinning each index to its token, plus a new regression test setting all four metrics to distinct values and asserting none cross-attribute.

Gate 8 re-verification: CLOSED. consistency-auditor empirically mutated a scratch copy of kSparkMetricTokens[] (swapped WatchRejected/Quarantined) and confirmed -fsyntax-only fails with a static_assert failure on exactly the two affected lines; grep-confirmed no literal [0-3] survives in the read loop; ran [spark][rollup][real]: 31/31 green. architect independently confirmed via a clean -fsyntax-only compile, calling the fix "strictly stronger" than its own Gate 3 recommendation.
